newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Merino rises at Christchurch NZ wool sale.
newsitem.headline: Merino rises at Christchurch NZ wool sale.

text.p: With the exception of fine merino, wool prices were level to slightly cheaper at the Christchurch sale on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The total offering was 1,997 clean tonnes of which 23 percent was passed in after failing to meet growers' reserves.
The final indicators saw fine segment up 44 cents at 891 cents, medium down four to 510 and strong down four to 438 cents. The market indicator was unchanged at 480 cents.
The sale comprised four percent merino fleece, 10 percent halfbred, 43 percent crossbred, 13 percent second shear, nine percent bulky skirtings and 10 percent crutchings.
Second shear bellies and pieces comprised four percent, with the balance in miscellaneous wools.

Compared with last week's sale, 19 micron merino was five percent dearer and 20 to 24 micron was unchanged. Halfbred was three percent cheaper on 25 micron, unchanged on 26 to 30 and one percent cheaper on 31 to 32 micron.

Crossbred was generally unchanged and second shear slightly cheaper. The main interest came from China and Western Europe with support from India, Turkey, Australia, Iran, the local mills and Japan. The next sale is at Napier and Dunedin on September 12. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
